newsitem.title: USA: US Treasury approves food exports to North Korea.
newsitem.headline: US Treasury approves food exports to North Korea.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury has issued a license allowing Minneapolis-based grain trading giant Cargill Inc. to export grain to North Korea, a Treasury spokesman said on Friday.
The export permission was the first U.S. move to improve ties with North Korea after Pyongyang expressed its regret late last month over the September submarine intrusion into South Korea.

"We have issued Cargill a specific license to export food to North Korea," the Treasury spokesman said. He could not give details on the exact amount of grain involved in the license granted to Cargill.

A company spokesman said on Monday it had applied to sell up to 2 million metric tons of grain to North Korea. The application did not specify rice, corn or other commodity, but it would be food, she said.
No comment was immediately available from Cargill on Friday.
Japan's Kyodo news service reported that the Treasury had approved the sale of about 500,000 tons.
Cargill is the world's largest private grain trading company.
The official North Korean news agency KCNA said on Monday the United States had pledged to ease a trade embargo against North Korea and give food aid to the communist state.
The reclusive North Korea has suffered from famine after two consecutive years of serious flooding.
